about: The embed and toolkit contract. The /embed/ addresses below are promised to keep working. scripts/embed/check-embeds.js checks every one in the build (run by .github/workflows/hugo.yml); /developers/ shows them; scripts/toolkit/build-toolkit.js reads toolkit and withheld. Edit with care.

embeds.title: Practice one topic
embeds.text: Problems for one ladder topic, checked as you go, with the lesson a tap away. Three right answers, the last two in a row, pass the topic.
embeds.params: topic: a topic id, like g3.add-within-1000 (pick one below)

embeds.title: Practice a whole course
embeds.text: The ladder’s own practice for one course: new topics in teaching order, mixed reviews and checkpoints.
embeds.params: course: a course key, like micro or alg1

embeds.title: Vocabulary word of the day
embeds.text: One word from the Vocabulary Ladder each day, the same for everyone, with its picture, meaning and memory hook.
embeds.params: word (optional): one word from the list, like indignant

embeds.title: Today’s Harvard Classics reading
embeds.text: The day’s fifteen-minute reading from the Harvard Classics, with a link to the full text.

embeds.title: Greek or Latin word of the day
embeds.text: One common word from the Gospels each day, the same for everyone: its dictionary form, meaning, a real form with its grammar, and a verse where it appears, with the King James Version English.

embeds.title: A short sentence drill
embeds.text: A few Latin or Greek sentences a day to hear, say back and understand, like the site’s Sentence Drills. Tap any word for its meaning and grammar. Gospel verses come with the King James Version; classical sentences with old public-domain translations.
embeds.params: lang: grc or lat · set: gospels (part of a Gospel passage each day) or classical (Caesar, Cicero, Virgil and Ovid in Latin; Herodotus, Homer and Plutarch in Greek)

embeds.title: Greek alphabet practice
embeds.text: Six short lessons, from the letters to reading real words from the New Testament, each with a quick quiz.

embeds.title: Write your name in hieroglyphs
embeds.text: Type a name and see it spelled with Egyptian sound signs in a cartouche, the way scribes wrote Greek and Roman names. Choose other signs, then save it as a picture.

nestle.name: Nestle 1904 Greek New Testament
nestle.by: Eberhard Nestle, editor (British and Foreign Bible Society, 1904)

macula.name: MACULA Greek
macula.what: Greek grammar (lemmas and morphology) and word-by-word glosses

vulgate.name: The Latin Vulgate Gospels
vulgate.by: Jerome (about AD 383), as edited in the PROIEL Treebank
vulgate.license: Public-domain text; the PROIEL edition is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0

proiel.name: PROIEL Treebank
proiel.by: the PROIEL project, University of Oslo
proiel.what: Latin and Greek grammar (lemmas, morphology, syntax), with the texts of the Vulgate, Caesar, Cicero’s Letters to Atticus and Herodotus

perseus-tb.name: Ancient Greek and Latin Dependency Treebank 2.1
perseus-tb.by: the Perseus Digital Library, Tufts University
perseus-tb.what: texts and grammar for Cicero’s Against Catiline, Virgil, Ovid, Homer and Plutarch

perseus-tr.name: English translations, from the Perseus Digital Library
perseus-tr.by: W. A. McDevitte & W. S. Bohn, E. S. Shuckburgh, C. D. Yonge, T. C. Williams, Brookes More, A. D. Godley, A. T. Murray and Bernadotte Perrin
perseus-tr.license: Public-domain translations; Perseus’s digital editions are CC BY-SA 4.0

lsj.name: Liddell–Scott–Jones Greek–English Lexicon
lsj.by: the Perseus Digital Library, with thanks to Tufts University
lsj.what: Greek dictionary for the classical sentences

whitaker.name: William Whitaker’s Words
whitaker.license: Free to copy, by the author’s terms

kjv.name: King James Version
kjv.by: 1611; the standard 1769 Oxford text, from the kjv package (npm), checked word by word against Wikisource’s transcription of the 1772 Oxford edition

phemister.name: Audio Greek New Testament
phemister.what: Greek audio, streamed from the Internet Archive
phemister.license: Free for non-commercial use with credit

voices.name: Your device’s own voices
voices.by: the text-to-speech built into the browser
voices.what: audio (Latin with an Italian voice, Greek with a modern Greek voice)

trb-cartouche.name: Cartouche maker
trb-cartouche.what: the spelling rules, sign choices and drawing

gardiner.name: Egyptian Grammar
gardiner.by: Sir Alan Gardiner (Oxford, 1927; 3rd edition 1957), and its Sign List
gardiner.what: signs, sound values and Gardiner codes

freeserif.name: FreeSerif, a subset
freeserif.license: GPL 3 or later, with the font exception

packs.name: Koine Greek: the four Gospels
packs.what: Every word of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John in Greek, with lemma, grammar code and gloss, and the Greek dictionary

packs.name: Latin: the Vulgate Gospels
packs.what: The four Gospels in Latin, with lemma, grammar and syntax for every word, and the Latin dictionary

packs.name: Classical sentences
packs.what: The sentence drills’ Latin and Greek sentences from Caesar, Cicero, Virgil, Ovid, Herodotus, Homer and Plutarch, with grammar and English, in files named for their source
packs.license: Per file: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 (PROIEL) or CC BY-SA 3.0 (Perseus); Greek dictionary CC BY-SA 4.0

packs.name: English: King James Version
packs.what: The KJV for every Gospel verse the embeds and drills use (936 verses)

packs.name: Greek alphabet tool
packs.what: The six alphabet lessons and quizzes, ready to open

packs.name: Cartouche maker
packs.what: Write a name in hieroglyphs, with the Egyptology model and fonts
packs.license: Code MIT; content CC BY-NC 4.0; TRB Hieroglyphs font SIL OFL 1.1; FreeSerif subset GPL with font exception

withheld.name: Hannah Ward’s Actual Reading lessons
withheld.why: shared on the site with her permission, which doesn’t yet cover embeds or downloads

left_out.name: Markets data
left_out.why: FRED and other data providers set their own terms

left_out.name: The ESV English
left_out.why: the site quotes 499 verses of the ESV under Crossway’s quotation allowance, which doesn’t cover embeds or downloads, so the embeds and the toolkit use the King James Version instead

left_out.name: The Greek audio recording
left_out.why: Marilyn Phemister’s reading is free for non-commercial use with credit; the Greek drill embed streams it from the Internet Archive with that credit, but it isn’t ours to bundle in a download

left_out.name: Art, Egyptology and Ancient Scripts ladders
left_out.why: they use artwork, fonts and images with their own licenses
